name: Emergency preparedness trivia (easy)
description: 25 questions drawn only from Nimrod's fact-checked course Practical emergency preparedness at home; each cites a page the course cites. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Practical emergency preparedness at home (Nimrod course) and the pages it cites

items.question: When a 911 call-taker answers, what does the course say to say first?
answers: Your full name and age
The address of the emergency
A short story of how it began
Your doctor's phone number
items.correct: The address of the emergency
items.explain: Help cannot be sent if the call-taker does not know where you are, so say the address first, before anything else.

items.question: If you call 911 by mistake, what should you do?
answers: Hang up right away and say nothing
Hang up and switch the phone off
Stay on the line and say it was a mistake
Hang up and call back later to explain
items.correct: Stay on the line and say it was a mistake
items.explain: Do not just hang up. If you do, the center may have to call you back or send someone to check.

source.title: What Happens If You Call 911 and Hang Up?

items.question: Why does a 911 call-taker ask so many questions?
answers: To test whether you really need help
To choose the type and level of help to send
To keep you busy until help is ready
To fill out forms before sending anyone
items.correct: To choose the type and level of help to send
items.explain: The questions are not a test. They help choose the right help, and in many centers help is sent while you keep answering.

source.title: Why does the 911 call taker ask so many questions?

items.question: What does the course say to do if you do not know the answer to a call-taker's question?
answers: Make your best guess so the call can move on
Stay silent until you are sure
Say you don't know, and share what you do know
Hang up and call again later
items.correct: Say you don't know, and share what you do know
items.explain: It is fine to say 'I don't know.' Don't guess or make something up.

items.question: What is the simple rule for choosing between calling and texting 911?
answers: Text if you can, call if you can't
Always text first, then call
Call if you can, text if you can't
Text twice before you try calling
items.correct: Call if you can, text if you can't
items.explain: The FCC says a voice call gives the 911 call center more information than a text does.

source.title: Text to 911: What You Need to Know

items.question: What does the course say about sending photos or videos in a text to 911?
answers: Send one photo of the scene first
Do not send them, because call centers cannot receive them
Send photos only of the home address
Send a short video if typing is slow
items.correct: Do not send them, because call centers cannot receive them
items.explain: Call centers cannot receive photos or videos. If you need to show something, describe it in words.

items.question: Where should copies of the one-page medical sheet be kept?
answers: Only in the person's wallet
Only as a photo on your phone
Only at the doctor's office
In more than one place, such as the fridge and the go-bag
items.correct: In more than one place, such as the fridge and the go-bag
items.explain: Keep one on the fridge, one in the go-bag, and a photo on your phone. Having more than one copy means someone else can find it.

source.title: Emergency Preparedness for Children with Special Health Care Needs: Emergency Information Form instructions for parents

items.question: How should you reach your local fire department to tell it that someone needing help getting out lives at your address?
answers: Call 911 and ask for the number
Call its non-emergency number
Wait until a fire has started
Text 911 with the details
items.correct: Call its non-emergency number
items.explain: Look up the non-emergency number first. 911.gov says not to call 911 just to get a non-emergency number.

items.question: In the recovery position class, what comes before anything else?
answers: Roll the person onto their side
Look up a first-aid book
Wait to see whether the person wakes up
Call 911 and follow the call-taker
items.correct: Call 911 and follow the call-taker
items.explain: The class says to call 911 first and to follow the call-taker over anything else in the class. Call-taker instructions do not delay the ambulance.

source.title: What to Expect When You Call 9-1-1 for a Medical Emergency

items.question: What do first-aid courses teach about a person who can cough forcefully?
answers: They should keep coughing while you stay close and watch
Give them back blows right away
Lay them flat on the floor at once
Give abdominal thrusts straight away
items.correct: They should keep coughing while you stay close and watch
items.explain: A person who can cough forcefully should keep coughing. Choking is when they cannot speak, cry or cough forcefully.

items.question: How often should each smoke alarm be tested?
answers: Once a year
Once a month
Once every six months
Only when it chirps
items.correct: Once a month
items.explain: Press the test button once a month. A loud beep, beep, beep means it works.

source.title: Smoke Alarm Information (Learn More About Smoke Alarms)

items.question: After how many years should a whole smoke alarm be replaced?
answers: 2 years
5 years
20 years
10 years
items.correct: 10 years
items.explain: Replace each smoke alarm 10 years after its manufacture date, which is printed on the back label.

source.title: Smoke Alarm Information (Learn More About Smoke Alarms)

items.question: During a power cut, where should a generator be used?
answers: In the garage with the door open
In the basement near the furnace
Just inside the back door
Outdoors, more than 20 feet from doors and windows
items.correct: Outdoors, more than 20 feet from doors and windows
items.explain: A generator makes carbon monoxide, which you cannot see or smell. Use it only outside, well away from the home.

items.question: How many ways out of each room does the escape plan suggest, where possible?
answers: One
Two
Three
Four
items.correct: Two
items.explain: If fire blocks one way, you use the other. A way out only counts if the person can really get through it.

source.title: How to make a home fire escape plan

items.question: What should you use for light during a power cut?
answers: Candles in every room
The glow of a TV screen
Flashlights, one for every person
A lit gas oven
items.correct: Flashlights, one for every person
items.explain: Use flashlights and not candles, because of the fire risk.

items.question: How much water per person per day does the Red Cross list for a kit?
answers: One cup
Half a gallon
Two gallons
One gallon
items.correct: One gallon
items.explain: The Red Cross gives water as one gallon per person per day.

source.title: Get a kit. Make a plan. Be informed. (Be Red Cross Ready factsheet)

items.question: How often does the CDC say to check your emergency kit?
answers: Every month
Every 2 years
Every 6 months
Every 5 years
items.correct: Every 6 months
items.explain: Check every 6 months so the contents are current and working. Replace old food, water, medicines and batteries.

items.question: What does a winter storm watch mean?
answers: Dangerous winter weather is arriving now
Dangerous winter weather is possible, so get ready
The storm has ended and roads are open
Only a minor winter event is expected
items.correct: Dangerous winter weather is possible, so get ready
items.explain: A watch usually comes first. It is your time to get ready before anything has started.

items.question: How far should space heaters be kept from anything that can burn?
answers: 6 inches
1 foot
At least 3 feet
At least 10 feet
items.correct: At least 3 feet
items.explain: NFPA's key rule is to keep space heaters at least 3 feet from anything that can burn.

items.question: What does Ready.gov say about fans in extreme heat?
answers: They cool a room as well as air conditioning
They are the best main way to cool down
They lower body temperature quickly
They move air but do not reduce body temperature
items.correct: They move air but do not reduce body temperature
items.explain: Fans create air flow and a false sense of comfort. Do not rely on a fan as your main cooling.

items.question: In a crisis, when many people are using phones at once, what does the FCC say about texts?
answers: Calls always go through before texts
Texts only work on landlines
Texts are always slower than calls
Texts often go through when a call will not
items.correct: Texts often go through when a call will not
items.explain: The course's advice is text first, talk second. Texts need much less bandwidth than calls.

source.title: Tips for Communicating in an Emergency

items.question: Why should the out-of-area contact live far away?
answers: So a call may get through when local lines are busy
So they can drive over quickly
So long-distance calls are free
So they know the neighbours
items.correct: So a call may get through when local lines are busy
items.explain: Local phone lines often overload after an emergency, and a long-distance call or text can be easier. Everyone in the household knows this person's number.

items.question: How often should you practise your home fire escape plan, at least?
answers: Once every five years
Only when you move house
Twice a year
Never, once it is drawn
items.correct: Twice a year
items.explain: The checklist says to practise the escape plan at least twice a year, including for someone who cannot walk.

items.question: Once everyone is out of a burning home, what should you do?
answers: Go back inside for pets
Go back inside for important papers
Wait just inside the front door
Call 911 from outside and stay out
items.correct: Call 911 from outside and stay out
items.explain: Get out, stay out, and call 911 from outside. Never go back inside for people, pets or things.

source.title: Fire Prevention Week: 20 Ways to Help You Avoid a Home Fire

items.question: Even if you sign up for the electric company's medical or priority list, what should you still do?
answers: Skip your own backup, since the list keeps power on
Plan your own batteries or other backup power
Stop checking your devices
Put away the flashlights
items.correct: Plan your own batteries or other backup power
items.explain: A registry does not promise power, so you still plan your own backup.

source.title: Emergency Power Planning for People Who Use Electricity and Battery-Dependent Assistive Technology and Medical Devices
